prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1148; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a side impact collision at an intersection. Insured vehicle was struck on the driver side by a vehicle that entered on a red signal. Police report requested. Claimant reports a concussion and is currently represented by counsel, so all contact is to go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Received the police report and two scene photographs from the insured. Both vehicles show damage consistent with a T-bone impact. Liability appears clear on the other driver. Sent acknowledgment letter to claimant's counsel confirming receipt of the representation notice and requesting medical authorizations and treatment records.

Entry 3: Counsel's office called to say the claimant was seen at an urgent care facility the day after the accident and was diagnosed with a concussion. Requested itemized bills and the initial exam notes. Noted that the claimant has missed several days of work and wants a wage loss statement from the employer.

Entry 4: Vehicle inspection completed at the body shop. Repair estimate received and reviewed for the driver side door, quarter panel, and airbag replacement. Estimate sent to the at-fault carrier for subrogation. Counsel was informed that the property damage claim is being handled separately from the bodily injury claim.

Entry 5: Follow-up with claimant's counsel. Medical records received showing ongoing headache and dizziness symptoms, with a referral to a neurologist. Counsel indicated a demand package will follow once treatment is complete. Diary set for review in thirty days and reserves reviewed for the bodily injury exposure.
